Create a new view INSIDE the CT scanner room, not the control room, much closer to the equipment. A physically recognizable enclosed modern CT gantry stands in the right half, off-white housing with a real circular patient bore, small realistic control buttons and indicator lights, floor pedestal and lateral thickness. A long narrow motorized patient table extends from the lower-left foreground into that bore. Generic fully covered adult patient lies supine under a blue-gray blanket, head toward the bore, no facial closeup, no staff. Three-quarter side-front view, all of scanner and bed visible, scanner/bed occupy center 80% so readable at 350px wide. Medium-dark but equipment brightly legible, cold-blue ambient and small warm light accents. Visible square pixel clusters, shaded textured machine housing, not smooth vector blocks, not abstract polygons, not photorealistic.
No words, logos, watermark, labels, beam rays, lasers, glowing radiation, arrows, UI, border, montage or multiple panels. This is one coherent high-resolution pixel game scene. Output landscape 1536x864 or 16:9.

images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: CT teaching atlas for BME game, a SINGLE square PNG with TWO evenly sized vertical image panels on black, separated by a narrow black gutter.
LEFT PANEL: plausible adult lumbar spine sagittal CT multiplanar reconstruction in BONE WINDOW, include T12, five lumbar vertebral bodies L1 through L5 and upper sacrum S1-S2. Five distinct lumbar bodies, normal overall lordotic curve, visible posterior elements/spinal canal, intervertebral discs, sharp cortical bone and trabecular texture; soft tissues muted gray. Sufficient field of view to see whole lumbar region, not an isolated vertebra.
RIGHT PANEL: adult pelvis coronal CT multiplanar reconstruction in BONE WINDOW, wide field of view with bilateral iliac wings, sacrum, both sacroiliac joints, acetabular roofs, both hip joints and proximal femora. Bilaterally plausible anatomy and scale, not a pelvis X-ray projection or transparent skeleton; actual cross-sectional grayscale CT appearance, soft tissue contour visible.
These are TWO DIFFERENT RECONSTRUCTION PLANES from the same waist/pelvis examination, separated into panels, never mixed into one anatomical slice. Depict no conspicuous displaced fracture, major deformity, blood, tumors or arrows. The game teaches reviewing COMPLETE bone-window axial and reformatted sequences, not declaring a diagnosis from these two pictures, so do not invent a highlighted lesion. Realistic CT grain and bone detail, high contrast bone window, grayscale only, black outside body. No patient identifiers, text, numbers, R/L markers, arrows, circles, scale bars, colored overlays, hospital logos or watermarks. Not pixel-style characters; this is a plausible radiological teaching image, square 1024x1024.
